name: Federal HPC
subtitle: DOE / NNSA / federal labs — tier-1 customer base

workload.typical_scale: 1,000 to 10,000 nodes per cluster at the lab tier; flagship systems (Frontier, Aurora, El Capitan) at 50K+ nodes.
critical_characteristics: Collective-heavy communication patterns (AllReduce, AllGather, AlltoAll)
Strong-scaling sensitivity
Long-running campaigns (days to weeks per job)
Multi-PI sharing with strict queue policies
workload.latency_budget: Sub-microsecond MPI message latency required; tail-latency variance matters more than median — a single straggling rank stalls the entire collective.
workload.bottleneck_profile: Network injection rate and collective tail latency at scale — endpoint NIC behavior under congestion is the differentiator, not raw bandwidth.
buying_criteria: Predictable tail latency
Mature MPI/libfabric stack
US-based supply chain (NDAA / Trade Agreements Act compliance)
10-year lifecycle support
Established federal procurement vehicle (GSA, SEWP, ITES)

descriptions: CN6000 at 800 Gbps per port; one NIC per compute node
Native OPA protocol — purpose-built for tightly-coupled MPI collectives
Director-class fabric switch with up to 576 ports for fat-tree topologies
architecture.protocol_reasoning: OPA over RoCEv2 for tightly-coupled HPC: 10+ years of MPI collective optimization, predictable tail latency under congestion, mature libfabric provider. RoCEv2 needs per-fabric DCQCN tuning with higher tail variance. UEC (CN7000) not production-ready for 2026-2027 federal cycles.

workload.typical_scale: 100 to 1,500 nodes per cluster (Stampede-3-class to mid-tier campus); multi-tenant fairshare scheduling; high job churn (10K+ jobs/day not uncommon).
critical_characteristics: Heterogeneous workload mix on shared physical fabric
Many short jobs alongside long campaigns
Multi-PI sharing under fairshare policies
Campus AI factories layered on existing HPC infrastructure
workload.latency_budget: Sub-microsecond MPI on HPC partitions and sub-millisecond AllReduce on AI partitions, served by the same fabric without cross-starvation.
workload.bottleneck_profile: Cross-partition resource contention more than absolute fabric performance — small ops teams (1-3 admins) can't tune dual fabrics, so single-fabric protocol flexibility outweighs raw throughput.
buying_criteria: Price-performance per NSF MRI / state funding dollar
Fabric versatility across heterogeneous workloads
Ecosystem breadth (Slurm + PyTorch both must work)
Operational simplicity for small staffs
ACCESS-allocation-compatible reference architectures

products: OPA or RoCEv2 mode (configurable per partition)
descriptions: CN6000 at 800 Gbps, protocol-configurable per partition
OPA for MPI partitions; RoCEv2 for AI partitions
Cost-optimized switch tier (Arista / commodity Ethernet, not director-class)
architecture.protocol_reasoning: Tri-protocol on one fabric is the academic differentiator: OPA preserves MPI performance (chemistry, climate), RoCEv2 serves AI training partitions. Academic budgets and 1-3 admin teams can't fund or run dual fabrics — single-fabric multi-protocol is where pure-InfiniBand and pure-Ethernet both lose.

name: Sovereign AI
subtitle: Nation-state and regional AI infrastructure — compliance, supply-chain provenance, vendor independence

workload.typical_scale: 200 to 2,000 nodes per deployment; multi-year commitments tied to national program timelines (3-5 year horizons typical); often phased pilot → expansion → full-scale.
critical_characteristics: Data residency requirements (workload and storage stay within national borders)
Supply chain provenance (NDAA / Trade Agreements Act / EU procurement compliance)
Vendor independence from US-China tension axis
Regulated procurement timelines (12-24 months typical)
workload.latency_budget: AI training collectives — not latency-pathological but throughput-sensitive; regional-language fine-tuning workloads tolerate slightly higher AllReduce latency than tier-1 frontier-model training.
workload.bottleneck_profile: Procurement timeline (regulatory approvals) and supply chain provenance dominate over raw fabric performance — the bottleneck is getting the contract through compliance review, not the network.
buying_criteria: Supply chain provenance (US-based or allied-nation, NDAA-clean)
Long-term roadmap visibility (3-5 year procurement requires confidence in the vendor's product roadmap)
Protocol independence (avoid NVIDIA lock-in for strategic reasons)
Local presence: regional support, language, time-zone coverage

descriptions: CN6000 at 800 Gbps RoCEv2 — sovereign AI is training-dominant, not MPI
NDAA-clean supply chain meets allied-nation sovereign procurement requirements
Region-dependent: Arista in EU, NTT/Hitachi-supported tiers in APAC. Pairs with regional integrator switch/server tier — named local partners required.
architecture.protocol_reasoning: Same RoCEv2 fit as Enterprise AI, but the value prop differs structurally: NDAA-clean supply chain (Chinese-origin alternatives can't meet allied-nation procurement), vendor independence from NVIDIA stack, and UEC alignment as a hedge against US export controls. Protocol independence here means buyer audit-ability — sovereign programs must inspect the fabric stack, which InfiniBand makes harder.
